metadata.scope: Every currently registered modifying handler; static signals are not proof. Manual priority screening is separate.
limitations: No tool was invoked. No native Blender acceptance or authorization bypass conclusion is inferred.
Registry/executor entry gates still apply when a handler discards context; this inventory flags missing domain-level access to fresh consent/recovery services.
Imported helpers, instance methods, callbacks and native operator behavior require follow-up review and adversarial native tests.
Source is a dirty development worktree and may change concurrently; each handler/file has a captured hash.

manual_review.scope: Read-only static inventory plus prioritized manual source screening; no safe verdicts.
manual_review.registry_inventory: 184 modifying handlers, including183 remote and1 local recovery tool, from247 total/246 remote registered tools.
secondary_triage: materials.py constructor/delete/slot/copy snippets and ownership-helper calls
simulation.py cloth_add/configure and contrast with existing cache guard
tool_registry.py and executor.py central permission/lifecycle flow
not_claimed: No complete manual per-tool audit for all184 handlers.
No native adversarial proof of these proposed next-increment scenarios.

No inference that a visible guard signal proves shared/linked/override, recovery or cancellation correctness.
manual_review.central_gate_correction: ToolRegistry.prepare already checks permission providers before pause/emergency flags. The ordinary real registry entry path has these gates; domain gaps concern subsequent writes and recovery. Additional custom-provider callbacks after prepare require a new frozen-state check.

findings.observed_gap: Automatic binding recovery snapshots group/modifier names and parent/world matrix, but has no snapshot or restoration/readback of pre-existing vertex memberships.

evidence.observation: _bind_automatic records existing names, parent and matrix; failure cleanup removes names not in those sets at lines717–724.
The public handler discards ToolContext and calls this native operation without a domain cancellation gate.

findings.risk_to_prove: If ARMATURE_AUTO changes existing deform weights before failing, removing newly named groups/modifiers cannot recover their previous values. Name-based cleanup may also include a foreign allocation.
findings.next_bounded_increment: Define explicit mesh/armature/dependent-consumer scope; capture bounded existing memberships, locks, modifier identities, parenting and context; add live gates and exact owned-allocation tracking; report any unrecovered native result honestly.
adversarial_scenarios: Existing deform groups with nonuniform weights plus a locked protected group; inject failure after native parent_set has modified existing weights.
Pause, permission revocation, cancellation or disconnect after native return; no unauthorized cleanup or late rewrites.
A native callback adds a differently identified group/modifier with an old/new name; automatic cleanup must preserve it.
Manual parent/weight changes interleaved with recovery; compare full memberships and sampled deformation before/after.

findings.observed_gap: These priority handlers discard ToolContext. Their domain writes and compensation therefore do not directly use its cancellation/permission/checkpoint services after initial registry/executor preparation.

evidence.observation: Bone updates perform multiple Edit Bone setters at lines444–460 with no retained context.
Constraint assignment delegates to context-free apply_assignments.
apply_assignments writes prevalidated fields, then attempts every saved old field on failure without a live gate, exact identity/configuration CAS or rollback readback.
Modifier assignment uses the same context-free batch helper.

findings.risk_to_prove: A stop or changed ownership/configuration during a native setter or partial failure can leave later writes/recovery outside the originally reviewed state. Initial entry authorization is present and is not being called a bypass.
findings.next_bounded_increment: Introduce domain-specific frozen object/child/dependency snapshots and per-write guards; make generic RNA compensation accept an explicit live boundary and expected output rather than blindly replay old fields.
adversarial_scenarios: Revoke the relevant permission or cancel between the first and second RNA assignments.
A failed setter partially writes, then a callback makes a newer manual edit; compensation must preserve that edit.
Replace the owner or named child with a same-name/different-session ID before the next write/removal.
Acquire a protected consumer after preflight; refuse subsequent writes and measure retained effects.

findings.observed_gap: Single-user/local object-data checks exist, but the reviewed legacy paths do not enumerate and freeze skinned meshes, Action/driver paths, bone-parented objects, constraints or other incoming consumers affected by rest-bone or pose edits.

evidence.observation: _edit_armature checks single-user armature data and changes mode/selection, without explicit dependent consumer closure.
Bone rename/parent/head/tail/roll/deform/connect setters run as one sequence.
Bone removal optionally reparents children and removes the bone, returning only local hierarchy facts.

findings.risk_to_prove: Single-user Armature data does not by itself prove that dependent skins or protected animation are unchanged by a rest-bone rename/removal or pose constraint.
findings.next_bounded_increment: Add explicit affected/protected rig consumer scope and complete rest/pose/hierarchy/animation snapshots; prove or reject rename/removal side effects across dependent objects.
adversarial_scenarios: A skinned mesh plus protected skin, bone-parented prop, shared Action slots and custom-property driver targets.
Rename a deform bone and inspect weight group names, F-curve paths, constraint subtargets and sampled deformation.
Remove a connected parent while preserving/reparenting children; inject failure after the first child change.
Linked/override consumers and hidden nested collections must be rejected or explicitly included.

findings.observed_gap: Both paths apply native geometry mutations with local/single-user/unkeyed checks, but no domain live boundary, bounded before/after geometry/dependency comparison, measured recovery or native blocking/cancellation evidence in the handler.

evidence.observation: transform_apply switches context and invokes bpy.ops.object.transform_apply.
modifier_apply resolves any named modifier, changes selection/active state and invokes the native operator.
preserved_object_context unconditionally restores mode/selection/active state in finally and suppresses RuntimeError/ReferenceError; it has no live owner/configuration comparison.

findings.risk_to_prove: Protected dependency output and recovery after a partial native topology operation are not established by FINISHED, and blind context restoration can overwrite a newer manual selection/mode.
findings.next_bounded_increment: Freeze exact modifier, source mesh/custom data and dependent consumer scope; classify reviewed modifier types; preserve context by identity and expected temporary state; retain partial native edits with explicit measured recovery rather than inferred success.
adversarial_scenarios: Apply a topology-changing modifier with UVs, colors, weights and protected incoming Geometry Nodes/Object Info consumers.
Failure/cancellation during native return or context restoration; record native blocking interval and retained geometry.
A frame/depsgraph callback changes selection, mode or active object; preserve the newer state.
Modifier replacement under the same name between lookup and application; no replacement may be applied.

findings.observed_gap: Exception cleanup removes newly allocated Object/Armature/Material IDs without a ToolContext deletion check or a frozen check that the allocation remains unconsumed and owned.

evidence.observation: create_rig removes the armature object with do_unlink=True and removes its data when users==0 after setup failure.
create_material allocates before diffuse-color coercion; its except path removes the Material ID.

findings.risk_to_prove: The repository policy requires DELETE_OBJECTS for data-block deletion. Cleanup should not implicitly unlink an allocation that acquired another consumer.
findings.next_bounded_increment: Use the already established retain-for-explicit-recovery policy, or require live deletion permission and exact unpublished allocation/consumer proof before deleting it.
adversarial_scenarios: Grant creation permissions but deny DELETE_OBJECTS, then inject a setup failure after allocation.
Acquire a protected consumer before cleanup and verify that the ID and consumer remain unchanged.
A same-name replacement must never be deleted; retain identity and source fingerprints in the failure record.

findings.observed_gap: The simple legacy weight paths do not read ToolContext. _apply snapshots memberships and replays them on failure without live consent, group identity/lock/value CAS, or independent restoration readback.

evidence.observation: _apply writes each membership, then restores all before records on exception. rollback_performed reflects only whether restore setters raised.
assign validates group lock once then calls _apply without context.

findings.next_bounded_increment: Reuse the newer bounded weight brush ownership/recovery contract for assignment/normalization and group allocation, with measured per-membership output and no stale recovery.
adversarial_scenarios: Manual group rename/reorder/replacement or lock changes between writes.
Permission denial, cancellation and memory failure after a subset of 32000 possible normalization memberships.
Restore setters return without preserving exact weights; rollback must be measured rather than assumed.

findings.observed_gap: The cache lifecycle has a live guard, but cloth allocation/configuration do not read their context and configuration uses the context-free generic RNA batch helper.

evidence.observation: cloth_add creates a modifier and sets quality without a domain live boundary.
configure checks baked/external/disk state once and applies prepared settings through apply_assignments.

findings.next_bounded_increment: Extend the cache guard principles to constructor and settings writes, including cache invalidation ownership, exact settings expectations and truthful partial allocation recovery.
adversarial_scenarios: Cache becomes baked/external, modifier is replaced or target acquires protected consumers after preflight.
Stop/cancel between modifier allocation and quality assignment, or between settings setters.
Failed configuration must preserve newer manual cache/settings edits and report whether invalidation occurred.

findings.observed_gap: Existing material ownership helpers are present, but these legacy handlers discard context; initial ownership checks do not by themselves establish live per-write/recovery preservation for nested/shared consumers.

evidence.observation: Deletion measures usage/ownership then removes the ID without a fresh domain boundary.
Slot edits perform data/material assignment and active slot changes without retained context.
Material copy-for-object isolates OBJECT binding; this existing protection must be retained while adding live scope checks.

findings.next_bounded_increment: Complete the broader material lifecycle gate with exact nested group/image consumers, slot identity/source snapshots and explicit owned allocation recovery.
adversarial_scenarios: Shared mesh DATA versus OBJECT slots with protected objects and nested shader/image consumers.
Permission revocation or new consumer before ID removal/slot replacement.
Partial binding/copy failure plus manual slot changes; identity-preserving measured recovery.

findings.observed_gap: Permission consistency needs a documented policy decision, rather than an assumed bypass conclusion: binding writes vertex weights with EDIT_ANIMATION+TRANSFORM_OBJECTS while weight tools use EDIT_MESH; applying transforms changes mesh coordinates with TRANSFORM_OBJECTS.

evidence.observation: rig.bind_mesh declares EDIT_ANIMATION and TRANSFORM_OBJECTS.
Weight modifying handlers declare EDIT_MESH.
Transform application shares TRANSFORM_OBJECTS metadata.

findings.next_bounded_increment: Resolve and document the authoritative capability model, then align Blender/MCP metadata and denial fixtures without silently breaking compatibility.
adversarial_scenarios: Deny EDIT_MESH while permitting rig/transform edits and verify the explicitly documented boundary for weights and applied geometry.

manual_review.release_gate_status: Full ownership/recovery audit and mandatory release acceptance remain open.
